gloss: to call out to someone; to speak to; to invite along

definitions.gloss: to call out to someone; to speak to someone first
definitions.explanation: To address someone who was not already talking with you — to get their attention, greet them, or offer help. The person is marked with に.

definitions.gloss: to invite along; to let someone know about an occasion
definitions.explanation: To ask someone to join an outing, a project, or a team. Common in {今度|こんど}{声|こえ}をかけてね, 'let me know next time.'

examples.japanese: {困|こま}っている{人|ひと}に{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I spoke to someone who seemed to be in trouble.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{人|ひと}にいきなり{声|こえ}をかけられて{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was startled when a stranger suddenly spoke to me.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}に{迷|まよ}っているようだったので、{思|おも}い{切|き}って{声|こえ}をかけてみた。
examples.english: They looked lost, so I worked up the nerve to call out to them.

examples.japanese: {今度|こんど}{飲|の}みに{行|い}くとき{声|こえ}をかけてね。
examples.english: Give me a shout next time you go out drinking.

examples.japanese: {何人|なんにん}かに{声|こえ}をかけたが、{都合|つごう}がつく{人|ひと}はいなかった。
examples.english: I asked several people, but none of them were free.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいプロジェクトを{始|はじ}めるにあたって、{経験|けいけん}のある{同僚|どうりょう}に{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: In starting the new project, I approached a colleague with experience about joining.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {声|こえ} (voice) + を + かける (to cast, to apply).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜に{声|こえ}をかける: to speak to ~, to invite ~
- {声|こえ}をかけられる: to be spoken to (the passive is very common)
- {声|こえ}をかけ{合|あ}う: to look out for one another by speaking up
- お{声|こえ}がけください: please let me know (polite; the noun form {声|こえ}がけ)

USAGE:
Sense 2 is a soft way to ask to be included — {声|こえ}をかけてね leaves the other person free to decide, unlike a direct {誘|さそ}ってね. In disaster-preparedness and workplace-safety contexts, {声|こえ}かけ is a set term for checking on the people around you.

cross_references.label: a woman picking up a man (for a date or hookup)
